issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a class named 'Stock' (with methods add, take, findStockIngredient, addToStockIngredients, emptyStock), but the provided template implements these methods in a class named 'Inventory' and leaves Stock.java empty. The solution also uses Inventory as the saloon's stock. This class-name/type mismatch (Stock vs Inventory) is structural and will confuse students about which class they must use or modify, and the empty Stock.java in the template prevents implementing the design as described in the statement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the class names consistent across artifacts. Either rename the provided Inventory class to Stock (update template, tests, and problem statement references), or update the problem statement and UML to refer to Inventory instead of Stock. Also ensure template Stock.java is removed or implemented consistently so students clearly know which class to modify/use.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a class named 'Stock' (the shared inventory for ingredients), but the provided template and the solution use a class named 'Inventory' to implement the same responsibilities. Additionally, Stock.java exists as an empty file in the repository. This mismatch between the conceptual name in the exercise description (Stock) and the concrete class name in the codebase (Inventory) is likely to confuse students: they will search for or expect a 'Stock' implementation as specified in the task but find an 'Inventory' class (and an empty Stock.java), making the mapping between the requirement and the template/solution unclear.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier for the shared ingredient container across all artifacts. Preferred fix: rename the Inventory class and its usages to 'Stock' (or provide a Stock class delegating to Inventory) so the code matches the problem statement and UML. Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to refer to 'Inventory' instead of 'Stock'. Ensure Stock.java is either implemented or removed to avoid an empty placeholder.
